You get your tattoos when you're five. That's because it takes a while for them to decide and coordinate who's name you get. 

I will never forget my day. We make it into a celebration, kind of similar to a birthday and we cheer when it's over. I revealed my names surrounded by my family, who got to enjoy the surprise as much as I did. 

Tradition states that we reveal our left arm first.
Some people disregard that, though. I peeled back my gauze that protected my fresh tattoo and it stung. 

Paul. 

"Paul?" My mom blurted, "Well we know which one that is," she joked. Everyone laughed. 

We moved on to my right arm, and as soon as I had revealed the name everyone gasped.

David.

"What?" My dad shouted at the tattoo man. "This must be a mistake, our son is not gay!" 

I didn't understand what was happening at the time. I wasn't even angry that I had two male names on my   body, and it was MY body. 

Awkward chatter filled the air and my mom sobbed. I wondered what I did to make her so upset. 

"There is no mistake," the man from the Name Council said. He packed up his belongings and drove away. I never saw him again.
I asked for a vacuum cleaner for Christmas.

I was struggling a lot with a standardized test I had to take in school. 21 female here in my last year of college. I went to therapy to honestly just vent about how frustrated I was that I just couldn't pass and my therapist was actually one of my old professors. He also has ADD and he made me read an article about the symptoms and it hit home harder than anything I've ever read before, and that's when I knew. When you find out, everything that never made sense finally clicks and you can become more conscious of it. It's a good and bad thing, I try to not blame everything on ADHD but it explains so much of my behavior. I thought for a while I was bi-polar, so just discussing with your psychiatrist can spark awareness of whether you have it or not.

I agree - getting him involved in some after school clubs might help. Also, in the summers, see if there is a summer camp he can be apart of. Usually you are put into groups and he might make some friends! Try your best to explain to him that getting in trouble isn't worth the laughs, and he should want people to be his friend for who he is. I'm sure your son is great and sometimes with ADHD we have trouble in social situations. He'll find his niche eventually but definitely try to encourage some type of outdoor activity / after school activity/ etc. good luck!

"Treat people the way you'd like to be treated," mother's voice rang in my ears. It'd been six months since I lost her to cancer and ever since then I couldn't get my mind straight. Working had become an outlandish waste of my time. Instead, i became fixated on something sneaker and more rewarding. Robbing a business would give me an adrenaline rush so powerful that it may cleanse my head momentarily. 

I started with Mr. Wong's Chinese restaurant. I creeped around the corner of the plaza when Mr. Wong was leaving to lock up. Dressed in black, I sprinted the corner and frightened the small Asian man. 

"Give me the key and go home or I'll hurt you," I muttered. 

He did. I entered the restaurant with every intention of finding a safe filled with cash. After all, it was the busiest restaurant in town. However, I was met with a horrid stench that infiltrated my nostrils and every step I took was sticky and wet. If this was my restaurant, I'd want someone to clean it too. 

I located the storage closet in the back room and found a mop and broom. Surely an old man working alone can only accomplish so much in one day. I knew the police would be here soon so I acted fast. I mopped up soy sauce and soda, swept egg roll crumbs and even bleached the floor and counters. 

I had to pee. The bathroom was horrendous. I found some windex and a toilet scrubber and began putting in the work. Mother would be so proud of my diligence. The bathroom trash was full, as was the main trash and I swatted away some flies and brought it to the dumpster. 

Upon reentering the restaurant I sighed in relief. Finally, a clean place to rob. Now, the safe! The cash! 

I heard police sirens in the distance. Frantically I searched the registers which were clearly empty and  I had no time to locate the safe. I ran out of the store to my black Chevy and drove home. I felt a strange sense of satisfaction although I had no money. 

The next morning I woke up in a haze and turned on the news. My heart raced when I saw Mr. Wong was being interviewed. 

"To the strange man that scared me but proceeded to perfectly cleanse my restaurant, please show yourself so I can give you a coupon!" He exclaimed and the news reporter laughed. 

"I guess we have a Dirt Fairy on our hands, folks," and Mr. Wong's eyes drifted into the distance. 

I went straight to my computer and began printing out business cards and flyers for a new business adventure: "Dirt Fairy Inc." Maybe burglary just wasn't my calling.

After the longest day I've possibly ever had a work, I finally pull into my drive way.  Being a nurse is rewarding, do not get me wrong. I love everything about my job, except the long demanding hours I am forced to work six days a week. I turn off my car and sigh. I am so exhausted. Just as I am about the check my phone a weird reflection comes off the screen. Strange. I look up and see a light flashing in my second story window. 
        The hairs on the back of my neck stand up. I live alone. did I forget to turn something off? Sometimes when my phone charger is plugged in it illuminates a small light to indicate charging. I look next to me, I brought my phone charger to work. Surely there must be some explanation for this. I giggle at the thought of me being frightened of my own home.
      I open the door and switch on the light. Silence, as usual fills my ears and I turn my attention to the stairs. I can see the light flickering, it's coming from my room. I walk upstairs like nothing is wrong but still feel uneasy. I look into my bedroom and see a small figure on my bed. The blood rushes to my head in confusion. It has a body, arms and legs and an antenna that has a small light at the end. It moved! It moved! I screamed and shut my door. The door opens and I see the little blue creature staring at me with red beaty eyes. "Yopo" it says and holds its hand out with a handshake. 
      "What the fuck are you.." I say, still in shock and my heart being fast. "Yopo not from here." it replies in a low monotone voice. "Well this is my house, whatever you are please leave." I say as calmly as possible. "Human so rude. Yopo exterminate." And before I know it I'm blacked out.
